questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length 5 cm, 5 cm, and 8 cm. What type of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: It has exactly two equal sides, which makes it an isosceles triangle.

questions.stem: Which triangle has all sides of different lengths and all angles of different sizes?
questions.explanation: A scalene triangle has no equal sides and no equal angles.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 27 cm. What is the length of each side?
questions.explanation: All three sides are equal, so each side $= 27 \div 3 = 9$ cm.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of $60°$, $60°$, and $60°$. Which statement is true?

options.text: It must be isosceles but not equilateral

questions.explanation: Three equal angles of $60°$ means all sides are equal, so the triangle is equilateral.

questions.stem: In an isosceles triangle, the base angles are always:
questions.explanation: In an isosceles triangle, the two base angles (opposite the equal sides) are always equal.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm. What type of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: Since $3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5^2$, it satisfies Pythagoras' theorem and is right-angled. All sides are different, so it is also scalene.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of side lengths could NOT form a triangle?
questions.explanation: For a triangle, the sum of any two sides must exceed the third. Here $2 + 3 = 5 < 6$, so these cannot form a triangle.
